title: Why the heart is called lev: thirty-two paths from the mind, and the will felt even in the breath
overview: Chapter 32 brings the end of the world of the *Ein Sof* down to the outer vessels of *Zeir Anpin*, the "upper man" on the throne, and explains it from man. In the soul, the will and delight of *yechida* are beyond any vessel, yet they shine, hidden, into the brain and from it into the heart; the heart's love and hate are themselves a will. The will reaches the heart along the 32 paths: *daas* opens into the brains of *chesed* and *gevura*, four brains of eight rooms each, and that is why the heart is called *lev*. The fifty gates of *bina* are doors, still hidden in the mind; the 32 paths are roads, the arousal already on its way through *daas*. Before the mind's love becomes the heart's there is a withdrawal at the narrow of the throat, a change of essence, yet the heart's *middos* match the mind's exactly. And the essential will is felt even in the breath of the heart, as one thing. The classes turn the grid of brains into how one should think, and into a digression on the sixty-four brains of one who contemplates, whose mind is on fire.

sections.title: Zeir Anpin, the man on the throne, is still the end of the world of the Ein Sof
sections.summary: The "upper man" on the throne is *Zeir Anpin* of *Atzilus*, the *middos*, the root of the flow that gives life to the worlds. Even its vessels, down to the outer *Nehi*, still count as the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*.

phrases.he: (לב) ומעתה יש להבין בבחינת אדם העליון דאצילות שעל הכסא כו'
שהוא בחינת זעיר אנפין דאצילות שמקבל מבחינת נה''י דאבא ואמא כו'
וידוע שהוא ענין ובחינת המדות דאצילות,
שהוא עיקר ושרש להשפעת מקור למקור לחיי העולמות
phrases.en: That's really the creator of the world.

blocks.text: The "upper man" on the throne is *Zeir Anpin* (lit. the small countenance) of *Atzilus*, which receives from the *Nehi* of *Abba*: the *middos* of *Atzilus*, root of the flow that gives the worlds life. **That's really the creator of the world**: in many places, "G-d" means this, the man who sits on the chair.

phrases.he: ועדיין הוא סוף עולם האין סוף,
phrases.en: And really this is also still considered the end of the *olam ha'Ein Sof*.

phrases.he: משום דאיהו וחיוהי וגרמוהי חד
כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: In the last chapter.

phrases.he: על כן גם עד בחינת כלים דזעיר אנפין בבחינת חיצוניות דנה''י שבו כו', נחשב עדיין מסוף עולם האין סוף:

blocks.text: This is **still considered the end of the *olam ha'Ein Sof*** (the world of the Infinite). First it reached only the inner *Atik*, then *Arich*; now, the vessels of *Zeir Anpin*, called the Holy One, blessed be He, for "He and His causes are one." They are *mamash* the *gufa d'malka* (the body of the King).

sections.title: In man: the will above all vessels shines, hidden, into the brain and the heart
sections.summary: In the soul, *chaya* and *yechida* encompass and are not limited in any vessel; only from *chachma* down is there a vessel. Yet the will and delight shine, hidden, into the brain and from it into the heart, and the *middos* of the heart are themselves a will.

phrases.he: וביאור הדברים, הנה מבשרי אחזה כו', דבצלם אלהי״ם עשה את האדם כו', וכמו שכתוב בצלמינו כדמותינו כו'
דהנה אנו רואים בנפש האדם שבחינת חיה יחידה שבו, הוא בחינת מקיפין דנר''ן, שלמעלה מהגבלת האורות בכלים
והוא בחינת הרצון והתענוג העצמי הפשוט שבבחינת יחידה, וגם בחינת פנימית ומקור השכל שנקרא משכיל, שזהו בחינת מקיף דחיה
בלתי מוגבלים בכלי כלל
רק מהחכמה ולמטה נמשך בכלי
והוא הנשמה שבמוחא, ורוח בלב כו'

blocks.text:
"From my flesh I see G-d": man is in the image of G-d. In the soul, *chaya* and *yechida* are *makifim* (encompassing levels), not limited in vessels: the essential will and delight of *yechida*, and the source of intellect, the *maskil*, of *chaya*. Only from *chachma* down is there a vessel: the *neshama* in the brain, the *ruach* in the heart.

The inner *chachma* is unlimited, and by the way, so is the inner *bina*: some places call *chachma* and *bina* together *chachma*, and *Yisroel Saba* and *tevuna* *bina*, so the inner *bina* is up there too.

phrases.he: והנה עם כל זה מאיר אור המקיף דרצון ותענוג, מבחינת פנימית אור החכמה בנר''ן שבג' כלים מוחא ולבא כו',
phrases.en: You see that the *ratzon* is *meir* in them, even though it's not *mugbal* by them.

phrases.he: מן ההעלם
phrases.en: In a hidden way.

phrases.he: והוא גלוי הרצון שבא בשכל וטעם גלוי, בבחינת מוח החכמה שנקרא אור אבא
phrases.en: That's where the *sechel* already comes in a *taam galui*.

phrases.he: ומשם נמשך ומתפשט בבינה, שהוא ההשגה
ומבינה שבמוח נמשך התפעלות המדות בלב

blocks.text: Still, will and delight shine into brain and heart: the *ratzon* (will) **is *meir* in them, even though it's not *mugbal* by them**, in **a hidden way**. In *chachma*, *Abba*, **the *sechel* already comes in a *taam galui*** (a revealed reason), then spreads into *bina*, and from *bina* come the *middos* of the heart.
The *middos* of the heart are really a will: love is a will for something, hate a will against it. *Ahava* (love) is *ava*, "he wants", with a *hei* in it.

sections.title: Thirty-two paths: four brains of eight rooms, tilting toward chesed or gevura
sections.summary: From *bina* the will travels to the heart along the 32 *shvilin* (paths). *Daas* opens into two brains, *chesed* and *gevura*, making four, each with eight rooms; the 32 rooms are why the heart is called *lev*. Every thought is placed by direction: front or back, up or down, right or left.

phrases.he: דהיינו מל''ב חדרים שבמוח שנקרא ל''ב שבילין דבינה
דמתפתחין להיות מוחין לזעיר אנפין כו'
phrases.en: They travel all the way down to *Zeir Anpin*.

blocks.text: From the 32 rooms in the brain called the 32 *shvilin* (paths) of *bina*. Elsewhere they are the 32 *netivos* of *chachma*; here he means the inner *bina*.

blocks.question: Is this because, as in *Derech Chaim*, there are two sets of 32 paths: one from *chachma* to *bina*, the *shvilin*, and one drawn from *Arich* into *chachma*?
blocks.text: The same one. As learned before, where it comes from in *Arich* is where it is in *chachma*: from the *mazalos*, in *Chabad* of *Chabad*; from the *middos*, in the *middos* of *Chabad*. As the asker said, it doubles into 64. The *shvilin* of *bina* are the inner *bina*, which is in *Arich*.

blocks.title: Route 66
blocks.text: A *shvil*, like a *nesiv*, is a road from one place to another, like Route 66 in the song, through St. Louis, down to Missouri, to Oklahoma. These 32 paths go from inside out and from outside in. **They travel all the way down to *Zeir Anpin***, which is why it is called *lev* (heart).
Now he explains the 32 *shvilin* of *bina*. By the way, this is chapter 32, *lamed-beis*, which is also *lev*.

phrases.he: כי המוחין נחלקים לד', חכמה ובינה וחסד וגבורה
phrases.en: Because the *mochin* open up into four: *chachma*, *bina*, *chesed* and *gevura*.

phrases.he: וכל אחד יש בו ח' חדרים,
phrases.en: Each one of these brains has eight rooms in it.

phrases.he: שהוא ל''ב

blocks.text: For **the *mochin* open up into four**: *daas* opens into two brains, since *daas* is the *memutza* (mediator) between *chesed* and *gevura*. These *chesed* and *gevura* are not *middos*; they are *mamash* brains. So instead of three brains there are four.

blocks.title: The cerebellum, a double brain
blocks.text: A doctor he sent this to told him the cerebellum is a double brain: it looks like one brain but, like the front brain, is really two, and they are not sure how it works. He does not know the particulars, but here it says how: it opens up into the two brains of *chesed* and *gevura*.

**Each one of these brains has eight rooms in it**, eight *chadarim*, 32 in all. Whether it is said here or elsewhere, he is not sure, but the eight rooms are the interweaving of *Havaya* and *Adnus*: the whole matter of the *sukka*, which has eight *sukkos* in it.

blocks.title: The square with a sukka on each corner
blocks.text: *Chachma*, *bina*, *chesed* and *gevura* make a square, not a cube. On each corner is a cube, eight points: a *sukka* on each. The whole square is the ceiling of the *sukka*, and the heart its floor, another square with eight rooms. That is why it is called *lev*.

blocks.title: The matrix: tic-tac-toe and the computer screen
blocks.text: And if you look at this, it is a matrix. What is a matrix? A tic-tac-toe.

blocks.title: The matrix: tic-tac-toe and the computer screen
blocks.text: A tic-tac-toe is a matrix three by three; this one is strange, a big square with little squares, where usually all the squares are the same. A matrix is like a tax table, bingo's B28, or the length and width of a chess board. A computer screen works as a matrix: the program tells it position 1,1 is green, 1,2 is green. Really it is simpler, only on and off; it cannot say red or blue. There are three colors: position 1,1 is red, 1,2 blue, and the third he does not remember.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 048 opens by finishing the matrix begun at the end of class 047, before it reads the chapter again from line 1.

phrases.he: והיינו הטעם שנקרא לב, מפני ששרשו בל''ב שבילין, הן ל''ב חדרים
שעל ידם דעת, שכולל חסד וגבורה, מטה אור השכל דחכמה ובינה להתפעלות לחסד וגבורה, כלפי זכות או כלפי חוב
phrases.en: So the *daas* is *mateh* it towards these two brains of *chesed* and *gevura*, and they actually *hispaalus*.

blocks.text: It is called *lev* for its root in the 32 *shvilin*, through which *daas* tilts the light of *chachma* and *bina* **towards these two brains of *chesed* and *gevura***, toward merit or guilt.

blocks.title: Jackie Mason's finger
blocks.text: This is also why Talmudic logic works as it does. Jackie Mason's finger goes to the right and to the left, and down and up, like a circle: right and left, front and back, down and up, the descent of *yud-kei-vav-kei*. Those are the rooms.

In general there are two in front and two in back. In thinking, the front is intellect and the back *middos*: an intellect of intellect, or of *middos*? And it goes up, toward *Havaya*, toward *Elokus*, or down toward the world, even as pure intellect. The *Chassidus* we are learning now is *davka* (precisely) intellect going up; the *iyun* (close analysis) of the Talmud is *davka* intellect going down.

Within that there is front and back, and right and left: in back *chesed* and *gevura*; in front *chachma* and *bina*, spreading out the whole or contracting the particulars, holistic intellect or "logistic" intellect. Each can go up or down. The back too, an emotion of spreading out, goes up or down: an intellect of emotions need not deal with emotions going down; it can belong above intellect altogether. Intellect going up goes above intellect; going down, below it.

So far the whole intellect is up; within it four intellects go up and down: in each, *chachma*, *bina*, *chesed* and *gevura* going up and going down. That is eight points. Each point has a room on it, a cube, one more whole thing like that; it keeps going, but he speaks of eight main rooms, each with eight points, like a *sukka*.

blocks.title: The man in the sukka
blocks.text: These eight points include everything. The man in the *sukka* does the *naanuim* (the shakings of the lulav), seven *middos*; seven times seven is 49, the *nun shaarei bina* (the fifty gates of *bina*). So the fifty gates and the 32 paths are one thing in different ways, including each other. And it is all going up: even the parts going down are in the brain.

sections.title: Fifty gates and thirty-two paths: the brain in bina and the brain in daas
sections.summary: The *middos* within the intellect, seven times seven, are the fifty gates of *bina*: doors, still hidden in the grasp. The 32 paths are roads: the beginning of the arousal travelling, through *daas*, from the mind into the heart. That is why the heart is called *lev*.

phrases.he: ונקרא גם כן מדות שבשכל, שהן בחינת ז׳ תחתונים דבינה, וכל אחד כלול מז',
phrases.en: So the *chesed* and *gevura* going back is also called the *middos* of the *sechel* of *bina*, which is *chesed* and *gevura*; it includes the whole *middos*, and each one is made up from seven.

phrases.he: שהן נ׳ שערי בינה
והכל ענין אחד,
phrases.en: It's all one thing.

phrases.he: רק שנ׳ שערי בינה הוא עדיין בהשגה דבינה, כמו חסדים המכוסים תוך יסוד אימא כו'

blocks.text: So **the *chesed* and *gevura* going back is also called the *middos* of the *sechel* of *bina***, each of seven: the fifty gates. **It's all one thing**, only the fifty gates are still hidden in the grasp of *bina*, before you even think. In the *Darkei Moshe*, say, the 32 paths already head toward the *pilpul*; the fifty gates are before that.

phrases.he: היינו בחינת התפעלות האהבה שבשכל והשגה עדיין, שנקרא מכוסה ונעלם בהשגה
phrases.en: It's really still completely hidden inside the *sechel*.

phrases.he: ואחר כך יוצא לגילוי מהות התפעלות מדת אהבה שבלב, שנקרא זעיר אנפין

blocks.text: This is love still in the grasp: **It's really still completely hidden inside the *sechel***. Then it comes out as love in the heart through the 32 *shvilin*, the paths from mind to heart. The fifty gates have another name.

blocks.title: A door, not a wall
blocks.text: A *shaar* (gate) is a door: something can come out of it, but nothing has to. The door goes nowhere; it is part of the house, an opening. So the hidden *middos* of *bina* are gates: unlike a wall, something can come out of them.

*Shaar* also means *shiur*, a measure in the mind of what the *midda* will be. As a listener said, it is hidden in the intellect: worked out logically in *bina*, like: if you had a brother, would he like cheese? Not an actual *midda*.

The 32 *netivos* differ. Their front is *chachma* and *bina*, but joined to the back, the brain of *daas*, so it is already the beginning of the arousal going down into the heart. A *nesiv* is a roadway: it actually travels somewhere.

blocks.title: Jackie Mason's thumb and the breakdancer
blocks.text: That is how you think: like Jackie Mason's thumb, not this point, then this point, but a flow. A mime, or breakdancing, is no flow: this point, then that point, a jerk. Those are points, each in its place, and a gate is like that: something can come out of it. A path is the thumb, a movement from one place to another: up to down, down to up, or side to side, "on the other hand", right to left, *chesed* one way, *gevura* the other.

This is really *daas*; the fifty gates are mainly *bina*, how the brain is in *bina*. *Chachma* and *bina* never part, and if there is no *daas* there is no *bina*, and if no *bina*, no *daas*. You cannot explain something to someone who will not listen and have him understand, nor come up with an explanation when you do not know what you are talking about. Without explanation, no knowledge.

You are not going to just sit and concentrate and have knowledge come. A *daas* that brings knowledge automatically, by itself, just because you are concentrating, cannot be: that is the whole business of *goyishkeit* (the non-Jewish way). There is no *bina*, there is no *daas*.

sensitivity.reason: Calls knowledge sought by concentration alone, without understanding, the way of goyishkeit.
sensitivity.publishable: You are not going to just sit and concentrate and have knowledge come. A *daas* that brings knowledge automatically, by itself, just because you are concentrating, cannot be. There is no *bina*, there is no *daas*.

blocks.text: They all work together, but the intellect is one way in *bina* and *chachma*, the front, and another in *daas*, the actual *hataya* (inclination) toward the thing. Chapter 2 said the *middos* come out of *tevuna*; but *tevuna* is a kind of *bina*, and nothing comes out of it without *daas*. Coming out to something outside itself is *davka* through *tevuna*, but the coming down into the *middos* is from *daas*. Why name *tevuna*, then? Because *daas* is basically the *middos*, their brain, but a brain, not yet a *midda*. So the fifty gates are the brain in *bina*, the 32 paths the brain in *daas*, *chachma* and *bina* included.

phrases.he: ועל דרך זה יוצאים ל''ב שבילין הנזכר לעיל בהתגלות מן התפעלות ההעלם שבמוח ללב,
ועל כן נקרא לב
phrases.en: That's why it's called a *lev*.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים בטעם שנקרא לב, מפני שמתקבצים שם ל''ב אורות דאבא ואמא, שהן ל''ב שבילין
(והן ל''ב ויאמר אלהי״ם דבינה שמקבל מאבא)
phrases.en: I think it says the 32 *Vayomer Elokim* in the creation of the world, which receives from *Abba*.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות.

blocks.text: So the *shvilin* come out from mind to heart: **That's why it's called a *lev***. Why name the heart for paths in the brain? The fifty gates are the brain as a brain; the *lev* is the brain coming into the heart, the *daas*, the arousal about to come out into the heart.

The *Etz Chaim* says it is called *lev* because the 32 lights of *Abba* and *Ima*, the *shvilin*, are bound there. He thinks they are the 32 times "And G-d said" in the creation, which receive from *Abba*: in *chachma* the 32 *netivos*, in *bina* the 32 *shvilin*.

Before going on, he goes over this as how you think, how the brain, which is what sees a world out there, grasps reality. First, in anything that comes up, the brain must decide: forward or back? A logical thing, *sechel'dik*, or an emotive one?

blocks.title: Did he bring flowers?
blocks.text: When your wife gets mad at you and has a reason, what do you do? An illogical person just shouts back. A logical person, with forebrains, first asks: is it really the logical reason that bothers her, or is it covering up something emotive, and really I did not bring her flowers for a while? And notice: at this point, not bringing flowers is not an emotion. It is an analysis, pure intellect, an intellect of an emotion.

sensitivity.reason: A husband-and-wife example in which the wife's stated reason covers up an emotional complaint.

blocks.text: So first decide: forward or back? Then: right or left? That places it on one of the four points of the square of your brain: forward, *chachma* or *bina*; back, *chesed* or *gevura*.

Within each are eight rooms: two forward and two back, and on top of them another two and two. So again: intellect or emotion? And up or down: placed in *chachma*, is it *chachma* going up or going down? Within *chachma* going up, is it *chachma*, *bina*, *chesed* or *gevura*? The *middos* of *Atik* are intellect going up: contemplating them has nothing to do with emotions, it is pure *hisbonenus* (contemplation), yet within it there can be *middos* too.

It goes down, then left and up: all kinds of combinations, like the synapses in the brain going from one to another. Each of the four points has eight rooms, and he goes no further. But a room has eight points and six directions, so already there are seven *middos*. And these are all intellects.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 049 opens by finishing the grid of the four brains and their rooms from the end of class 048, before it reads line 28.

blocks.title: The TV screen: a grid of on and off
blocks.text: What we have is a grid. Represent physical reality in two dimensions and you get a computer or TV screen, which is only yes, no, no, yes. A point on the screen cannot change colors, only go on and off; colors come from clusters of three points, red, blue and yellow (he is not sure those are the three). But here each point is not a point but a whole room.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 049 opens by finishing the grid of the four brains and their rooms from the end of class 048, before it reads line 28.

blocks.title: The little Aibershter with a lulav
blocks.text: Inside each room stands a little guy, a little *Aibershter* (the One Above, G-d) with a lulav, who can change it into the seven colors of the rainbow, since each *sefira* has a color. Six *naanuim* include seven *sefiros*: the seventh is when he brings it in to himself. Right is *chesed*, left *gevura*, forward *tiferes*, up *netzach*, down *hod*, back *Malchus*, to the west, and he himself, the lulav, *yesod*, "the *tzaddik* is the foundation of the world", who connects heaven and earth and the four directions. And it is three-dimensional, with zillions of these little guys.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 049 opens by finishing the grid of the four brains and their rooms from the end of class 048, before it reads line 28.

blocks.title: The cathode gun: one point at a time
blocks.text: But really there is only one guy. A TV has only one point: a cathode gun shoots light at a point, basically a *tzimtzum* and a *Kav*, and moves across, one point at a time. So how does the whole world exist? On a TV the point glows a little after the light leaves it. Does a point glow on after the *Aibershter* has gone? No: He moves so fast that He is in all places at once.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 049 opens by finishing the grid of the four brains and their rooms from the end of class 048, before it reads line 28.

blocks.text: Here it says *yesod* is west and *Malchus* the holy sanctuary in the middle. Usually *Malchus* is west, and all creation bows west because *Malchus* is there. This way is "Your kingship is the kingship of all worlds": *Malchus* is a *dalet*, spreading to the four directions and through all worlds. But *yesod* and *Malchus* are sort of interchangeable; either can be in the west.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 049 opens by finishing the grid of the four brains and their rooms from the end of class 048, before it reads line 28.

blocks.text: Usually *Malchus* is west, which is why the *Beis HaMikdash* went toward the west, and the little guy standing in the *sukka* is *yesod*, the *tzaddik*. "For all that is in heaven and earth": *yesod* connects the directions, heaven to earth, right to left, forward to back, since *shamayim* (heaven) is fire and water, and earth is *Malchus*. So he is called *kol*, all: he can make any color you want. *Malchus* is the final point you see on the screen; it has nothing of its own, only what *yesod* told it: green, then green; blue, then blue.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 049 opens by finishing the grid of the four brains and their rooms from the end of class 048, before it reads line 28.

blocks.text: That is the grid, and so your brain thinks: in directions. The physical directions come out of the emotional ones, these out of the intellectual ones, and these from directions higher up, all from the *Kav*. The grid goes into your heart too. Sit back and you feel a head, a heart and a bottom: your sense of up and down. Mainly head and heart, since the *Nehi*, the guts, are in the *Chagas*: the brain comes down into the heart.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 049 opens by finishing the grid of the four brains and their rooms from the end of class 048, before it reads line 28.

blocks.title: Sixty-four brains
blocks.text: He thinks a later chapter explains this as the matter of the *tzaddik*, and it comes *davka* through contemplation, which opens *daas* into two brains. In an ordinary person *daas* is one brain, emotion: with no *hisbonenus*, no analysis, it is arousal like an animal's, which is why one who does not contemplate is called an animal. He has three brains. In one who contemplates, *daas* opens into two, so he has four, and automatically 32; then the 32 paths go down into the heart and become 32 more, brains, not *middos*. Sixty-four brains: more than twenty times an ordinary person's, and that is only quantity.
blocks.outOfPlace: After reading line 28, class 049 stops the text and goes back to the 32 paths that go down into the heart: the sixty-four brains of one who contemplates.

blocks.title: Brains on fire, a cold heart
blocks.text: Then quality: the brains in his brain become hot and his heart cold. A cold-hearted person, like the song, "your cold, cold heart"? No: his *middos* do not boil over; they follow the intellect. But his intellect is no longer cold logic but a fire, so it is beyond comparison. He does not just receive light; he is a *maor* (a source of light), because it is *daas*: he is totally connected, totally interested. Even a little real *daas* is beyond comparison with ordinary thinking, and he has 64 brains on fire. The 32 brains in his heart are on fire too, so really his heart is on fire, and a brain's light is far more than a heart's. Only the outer, emotional heart is cold, so emotions cannot interfere. Usually the emotions burn and the brain is cold; by him the brain burns.
blocks.outOfPlace: After reading line 28, class 049 stops the text and goes back to the 32 paths that go down into the heart: the sixty-four brains of one who contemplates.

blocks.text: This is the actual arousal, and it comes only through contemplation: not what other people think, but the inner arousal we are going for. The outer kind, the crying, is also something, but nothing beside a man with sixty-four brains.
blocks.outOfPlace: After reading line 28, class 049 stops the text and goes back to the 32 paths that go down into the heart: the sixty-four brains of one who contemplates.

blocks.title: The sixty-fourth brain
blocks.text: A *talmid chacham* (Torah scholar) with more than a sixty-fourth of *ga'ava* (pride) is a *gas ruach* (coarse of spirit). *Gas* is sixty-three: he has only 63 brains, really three, and thinks he has 64. It also means the other way: lacking that sixty-fourth of pride shows he is a *gas ruach*, without the sixty-fourth brain, the main brain of *Chassidus*, pride with *Chassidus*: "his heart was lifted up in the ways of G-d".
blocks.outOfPlace: After reading line 28, class 049 stops the text and goes back to the 32 paths that go down into the heart: the sixty-four brains of one who contemplates.

blocks.text: When it comes to an attack on *Chassidus*, G-dliness, *Yiddishkeit* or the *Rebbe*, all of a sudden he is not five cents anymore. He turns into a werewolf, super haughty, and knocks the other guy down; and that, which most people do not understand, is the sign of humility. Humble about himself, about Reform and Conservative he will say flatly they are not rabbis and only he is right. It looks arrogant; but *davka* the one who does not get fired up at an affront to the *Aibershter* is the *gas ruach*, without the sixty-fourth brain.
blocks.outOfPlace: After reading line 28, class 049 stops the text and goes back to the 32 paths that go down into the heart: the sixty-four brains of one who contemplates.

blocks.title: Matisyahu and Mordechai
blocks.text: Look through history. Matisyahu was a humble little old man; when it came to it, he took a sword and killed the goy and the Jew in front of everybody, without a word. Mordechai, the *Rebbe*, was very humble; but when Haman came up, an affront to the *Aibershter*, "he would not bend or bow". The Jews told him he would make Haman mad; he did not care. (The tape ends as he quotes Matisyahu.)

sections.title: The narrow of the throat: a withdrawal before the mind's love becomes the heart's
sections.summary: For the *midda* in the mind to become a *midda* in the heart there must first be a contraction and withdrawal, like a seed that rots before it grows: the narrow of the throat of *bina*, like the membrane between the source of intellect and intellect, and the liver between the organs of breath and of food.

phrases.he: והנה ודאי כאשר צריך להיות התהוות התפעלות המדה בלב מן העלם התפעלות המדה בהיותה בשכל והשגה דבינה, הוצרך להיות תחלה בחינת צמצום והעלם וכיווץ שנקרא הסתלקות (כמו משל רקבון הגרעין בשביל השתנות ממהות למהות וכידוע)
והוא בחינת מיצר הגרון דבינה,
phrases.en: This is the *tzimtzum* between the brain and the heart, which is the throat, called the narrowness of the throat.

phrases.he: שנתעלם שם התפעלות השכל ונמשך להיות בשינוי המהות בהתפעלות הלב
(וכמו בחינת קרומא כו'
phrases.en: Which is between the *maskil* and the *sechel*.

phrases.he: שהוא המעלים ומפסיק מכח עליון שלמעלה מן השכל, לבוא לשינוי המהות בגלוי אור השכלה כו'
וכמו חצר הכבד
phrases.en: And then on a lower level is another place where the next *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: שמפסיק ומבדיל בין אברי הנשימה לאברי המזון להיות שינוי המהות וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות)

blocks.text: For the *midda* to come into the heart out of its hidden arousal in *bina*, there must first be a *tzimtzum* (contraction), a withdrawal, like the seed that rots to change from one thing into another. That is the *meitzar hagaron* (the narrow of the throat) of *bina*: **the *tzimtzum* between the brain and the heart**, where the arousal of the intellect is hidden and comes out as a *shinui hamahus* (a change of essence). It is like the *kruma* (membrane), **between the *maskil* and the *sechel***.

blocks.question: Is the separation he means the diaphragm?
blocks.text: No. Below the throat is another place of the next *tzimtzum*, the *chatzar hakaved* (lit. the court of the liver), which separates the organs of breathing from the organs of food. The diaphragm is not it: it is just the physical border, the end of the lungs, the thing that pushes the lungs in and out, and nothing passes through it. Where it goes over from one to the other there is a transformation, a change of essence, and that is in the liver, which is basically a filter.

sections.title: The heart's middos match the mind's exactly, and even their outer vessels are still Ein Sof
sections.summary: The *middos* in the heart come out exactly as they were in the mind, only changed in essence and limited by *netzach* and *hod* of *bina*, the "therefore" of the reasoning. Each has three levels and three vessels; even the outermost, the breath of the chest, is still the *Ein Sof*.

phrases.he: אך עם כל זה המדות שבלב הן בדומה ממש אל המדות שבשכל, ממש כאופני התפעלותם במוח,
phrases.en: Exactly how you think in the brain.

phrases.he: בלי נטיה כקוצו של יו''ד כידוע
רק שבלב באין בשינוי המהות ובהגבלה וצמצום דבחינת נצח והוד דבינה, שהוא שליחות שפע אור ההשגה בעצם,
בשביל התפעלות המדה לבד כידוע
phrases.en: It's not the *etzem*, it's only the *shlichus* for the *hispaalus hamidda levad*.

blocks.text: The heart's *middos* are like the mind's: **Exactly how you think in the brain**, to the tip of a *yud*. In the brain it is intellect, in the heart an actual *midda*, a change of essence; yet understand that someone is doing you good, and the love in your heart is as big as the love in your brain.
Only in the heart they come changed, limited by the *netzach* and *hod* of *bina*, which send the grasp for the *midda*: the *uvchein* ("and so"), so therefore I like the guy.

blocks.question: What does *b'etzem* mean here?
blocks.text: The very essence of the grasp, in *bina*. *Netzach* and *hod* are only its *shlichus* (sending), not the essence: **it's only the *shlichus* for the *hispaalus hamidda levad***, the arousal of the *midda* alone, the *uvchein*, the "therefore" of the intellect.

phrases.he: ובמדות שבלב כלול מג' מדריגות, חב''ד חג''ת נה''י
דהיינו בחינת המושכל ומורגש ומוטבע
הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: Same like we said before.

phrases.he: וג' כלים לכל אחד, פנימית ואמצעית וחיצוניות
phrases.en: And each one of them has three *kelim*.

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל באריכות
phrases.en: This was all discussed earlier.

blocks.text: The *middos* in the heart include three levels, *Chabad*, *Chagas* and *Nehi*: the *muskal* (the understood), the *murgash* (the felt) and the *mutba* (the instinctive), the **same like we said before**, and **each one of them has three *kelim***, inner, middle and outer.

phrases.he: אך הנה גם בחינת החיצוניות דכלים דנה''י שבלב - שהוא בחינת התפעלות החסד והאהבה שבלב כשבאה לידי השפעה לחוץ,
שנקרא נה''י דחזה
phrases.en: The lungs: the lungs are the external of the heart.

phrases.he: במחשבה דיבור ומעשה,
היינו על ידי חיצוניות הכלי דלב, שהוא בחינת המוטבע אשר בהבל החזה דזעיר אנפין דאצילות,
phrases.en: The *mutba* in the *chaze*: meaning that according to the *teva*, when you get upset, you start breathing hard.

phrases.he: שעל זה אמר איהו וגרמוהי חד
- הכל עדיין בבחינת אין סוף
phrases.en: Even down to there: even the fact that your lungs are breathing hard, it's still you, completely connected to you.

blocks.text: Even the heart's love going outward in thought, speech and action comes through the *mutba* in the breath of the chest, for **the lungs are the external of the heart**. When you get upset, by nature you breathe hard. That is not *muskal*, not even *murgash*, not the feeling that I like this guy; the *muskal* is still an *uvchein*, a "therefore", and this is a *mutba*.

blocks.title: The bull breathing fire
blocks.text: That is the breathing of the heart, like the bull breathing fire: the *mutba*, the *Nehi* in the breath of the chest. So anger is *charon af* (lit. the burning of the nose): when he gets mad, he breathes hard.

Of this *mutba* in the chest of *Zeir Anpin* it says "He and His causes are one": even there it is all still *Ein Sof*. In a person, **even the fact that your lungs are breathing hard, it's still you**.

sections.title: The essential will is felt in the breath of the heart, and so in Zeir Anpin: it is, and it isn't
sections.summary: In a person the essential will, after all its contractions, is felt even in the breath of the heart, as one thing with its source. So in *Zeir Anpin*: the simple will from before the first *tzimtzum* shines in the outer vessels of its heart, still the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*. Is it the Essence? It is and it isn't.

phrases.he: וכמו על דרך משל באדם התחתון כאשר הרצון העצמי שבבחינת מקיף דיחידה הנזכר לעיל, מאיר ובא בגלוי במוחין דחכמה ובינה, עד שיורד ומתצמצם בקטנות המוחין דכלי דנצח והוד דחסד מורגש שבלב, שהוא בהבל החזה
- הרי גם שם הרצון מאיר
phrases.en: Even there, the *ratzon* is still there; it's the same *ratzon*, even though it had to go through various *tzimtzumim*.

phrases.he: כי אנו רואים שבהבל הלב גם כן מורגש הרצון
phrases.en: So we see that even in the *hevel halev* the *ratzon* is *murgash*.

phrases.he: ונקרא רעותא דלבא,
phrases.en: It's called the *ratzon* of the heart.

phrases.he: מה שלבו חפץ במורגש לדבר טוב,
phrases.en: What his heart wants with actual feeling: not with intellect, and not even with the emotion, but the actual *hergesh* of it.

phrases.he: ולמאוס בהעדר הרצון בלב לדבר רע השנאוי כו'
phrases.en: Like for instance in fear, that he has a *hipuch haratzon* for this thing; he's trying to run away from it.

phrases.he: אם כן, מתאחד ומתקשר ממקור הרצון העצמי עד הבל הלב ברגע אחד,
כאילו הוא מהות אחד ממש
phrases.en: It's as if it's *mamash* one thing.

blocks.text: Even there the will shines: it is felt in the breath of the heart. Why is he getting mad? Because it goes against his will. This inner will is called the *re'usa d'liba* (the will of the heart), what his heart wants.
blocks.outOfPlace: He reads ahead from line 38 into lines 40-42 here, until a listener tells him he skipped a few lines and he goes back.

blocks.text: As in the lower man: the essential will of the *yechida* shines in the brains and comes down to *netzach* and *hod* in the breath of the chest, and **even there, the *ratzon* is still there; it's the same *ratzon***, through all the *tzimtzumim*, until he is breathing hard. The breathing shows there is a will.

blocks.title: The dog that wants food
blocks.text: You see it especially with a dog: when he wants some food, or wants something, he starts breathing hard.

**So we see that even in the *hevel halev* the *ratzon* is *murgash***: **the *ratzon* of the heart**, wanted not with intellect, not even with emotion, but with actual *hergesh* (sensation). And the opposite: in fear he has a *hipuch haratzon* (an aversion) and runs from the thing, or if they tell him to work.
So the source of the essential will is bound to the breath of the heart in one moment, **as if it's *mamash* one thing**, as if the will is in the heart.

phrases.he: והיינו דמיון להבין באדם העליון
phrases.en: And this is a *dimyon* to understand in the upper person.

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת זעיר אנפין
שבבחינת לב דזעיר אנפין נאמר ויאמר אל לבו, להטות לחסד
phrases.en: He told his heart *l'hatos l'chesed*, to be *noteh* towards *chesed*.

phrases.he: וכן ויתעצב אל לבו, לבחינת דין וכהאי גוונא
הרי בבחינת חיצוניות הכלי דנצח והוד דלב זה,
phrases.en: Meaning the actual feeling of the breathing of it.

phrases.he: מאיר שם מבחינת הרצון הפשוט העצמי שבעצמות אור אין סוף שלפני הצמצום הראשון
phrases.en: It's *mamash* the *ratzon*, the *ratzon atzmi*.

phrases.he: (הנזכר באות יו''ד בבחינת יחיד ואחד כו', במשל חפץ חסד העצמי בעצמות הנפש כו')
phrases.en: This is the *ratzon* which is talked about in chapter 10.

blocks.text: This is a likeness for the upper man, *Zeir Anpin*: "And He said to His heart": **He told his heart *l'hatos l'chesed***, to lean toward kindness; "He was saddened to His heart", toward judgement, at the flood. In the outer vessel of that heart, **the actual feeling of the breathing of it**, shines the essential will from before the first *tzimtzum*, change of essence or not: **It's *mamash* the *ratzon***, the will of chapter 10.

phrases.he: ואם כן עד בחינת חיצוניות הלב דזעיר אנפין נחשב עדיין הכל מסוף עולם האין סוף
משום דאיהו וגרמוהי חד,
phrases.en: He is one, one with his organs.

phrases.he: כמו באדם,
phrases.en: Like a person, he's *mamash* literally one with his organs.

phrases.he: שלבו ורצונו העצמי אחד הוא כו' ודי למבין:
phrases.en: That his heart, meaning also his lungs, and his *etzem haratzon* is one thing, *mamash* one thing.

blocks.text: So even the outer heart of *Zeir Anpin* counts as the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*, brought farther and farther down. First even the *machshava kduma* (the primordial thought) was past it; then it was part of it, and *Adam Kadmon* a new creation; then *Adam Kadmon* too; then inner and outer *Atik*, *chachma* and *bina*, the inner heart. Now even the outer vessels of *Zeir Anpin*, completely connected, as a scared person's breathing changes automatically.
"He and His causes are one": **He is one, one with his organs**, as a person is: his heart, his lungs too, and his *etzem haratzon* (essential will) are *mamash* one thing, the *gufa d'malka*.

So again, as in chapter 10, it is and it isn't. First it is not the *Ein Sof*: a *tzimtzum*, another *tzimtzum*, not even *chachma* and *bina*, then the narrow of the throat. So is it? Is it the real *Atzmus* (Essence)? No more than a person's outer vessels, just flesh, are really him. From the other side, of course it is him.

reviewQuestions.question: How can the vessels of *Zeir Anpin*, down to the outer *Nehi*, still be the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*?
How do four brains of eight rooms make the 32 paths, and why do they give the heart its name?
What is the difference between the fifty gates of *bina* and the 32 paths, and what has *daas* to do with it?
Why must there be a withdrawal at the narrow of the throat before the mind's love becomes the heart's?
If the heart's *middos* come with a change of essence, how can they match the mind's exactly?
What does breathing hard when one is angry or afraid show about the will, and what does it teach about *Zeir Anpin*?
